demo_answers: You are having Pernicious Anemia. It is due to deficiency of Vitamin B-12. It can not be treated by oral medication. So you need to take injections of vitamin B-12. Intrinsic Factor is produced by stomach cells. If it is deficient then you will not be able to absorb vitamin B-12 from food. So your doctor may order for intrinsic factor estimation also.

It is true that some infections can be treated in the outpatient setting, but if there are signs of infection such as fever, redness, swelling, pus, etc., then you should go back to the doctor. Infection is one of the most common reasons why people have to return to the hospital after being discharged.

As per your query you have symptoms of TMJ disorder which can be due to misalignment of teeth, clenching of teeth, grinding of teeth, arthritis, trauma etc. Need not worry. I would suggest you to consult oral physician once and go for thorough examination. Doctor may order x-ray of jaw and take impression of teeth. Doctor may prescribe muscle relaxant, analgesics, vitamin B complex, calcium supplements, soft diet, mouth guards, hot compresses, physiotherapy, topical anesthetic gel, anti-inflammatory painkillers like ibuprofen, acetaminophen, etc. Doctor may refer you to orthodontist for further treatment.

You should consult your doctor and get done clinical examination of penis and urine routine microscopy and culture. If needed you may need to take antibiotics.

You are having symptoms of alcohol induced gastritis. It can cause vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain etc. You should avoid alcohol completely. Take proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole or pantoprazole. Avoid hot and spicy food. Avoid junk food. Avoid stress and tension. Be relaxed and calm.

You should also take low fat diet. Avoid saturated fat, trans fat, junk food, butter, cheese etc. Take more fruits and green leafy vegetables.

You may need some investigations like thyroid profile, prolactin level, ultrasound of pelvis, follicular study etc. Based on reports, you may need medicines like camphene citrate, progesterone etc.

PFO (patent foramen ovale) is a congenital defect. It is present at birth. It is not associated with any disease. So it is not necessary to close it. If you want to close it then there are two options. First option is surgical closure of PFO. Second option is transcatheter closure of PFO. Both these procedures are safe and effective.
